title: "Decision map"
page-layout: full
toc: false
resources:
  - data/menu_options.csv
  - data/spec_curve.csv

```{r}
#| include: false
# Data for the decision map, read once at render: every option of the menu,
# the curve of the claim, every option of the curve against its twins, and the
# displays that hold the options off the curve at the reference settings. All
# of it is aggregate, and the twins are paired in the browser from the curve.
# readr rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "".

menu <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
# a column that holds only "t" would be read as logical without its type
curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                         col_types = readr::cols(stat_type = readr::col_character())) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange(c("b", "spec_id")) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(rank = 1:n())
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
displays <- readr::read_csv("data/display_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                            col_types = readr::cols(stat_type = readr::col_character()))
shares <- readr::read_csv("data/display_shares.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
analysts <- readr::read_csv("data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
score_file <- readr::read_csv("data/display_score_file.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
repro <- readr::read_csv("data/display_reproduction.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(curve) == 144, sum(curve$is_reference) == 1)

fallback_titles <- c(
  "cases/cohabitation/index.qmd" = "The cohabitation case",
  "cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd" = "Specification menu",
  "cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd" = "Multiverse",
  "companion/event-history.qmd" = "Event-history analysis",
  "companion/binary-outcomes.qmd" = "Binary outcomes",
  "companion/dags.qmd" = "Causal graphs and adjustment sets",
  "companion/weighting.qmd" = "Weights"
)
# page titles without their Markdown emphasis; a page not yet written takes
# the title of its navbar entry
page_title <- \(f) {
  path <- file.path("../..", f)
  title <- if (file.exists(path)) rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(path)$title
  title <- title %||% unname(fallback_titles[f])
  if (is.na(title)) f else gsub("*", "", title, fixed = TRUE)
}

# taught_on is a path from the project root, and the page links up two levels
menu_js <- menu |>
  datawizard::data_modify(page = taught_on) |>
  datawizard::data_select(c("axis", "level", "option", "label", "on_curve", "page", "reason", "decision",
                            "stage", "judgement", "phrase", "estimates", "explanation"))
pages <- unique(menu_js$page) |>
  purrr::set_names() |>
  purrr::map(page_title)

# the 95% interval of each specification on the t of its own df
curve_js <- curve |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    spec_id, cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model,
    b = round(b, 5), lo = round(b - stats::qt(0.975, df) * se, 4), hi = round(b + stats::qt(0.975, df) * se, 4),
    stat = round(stat, 3), df, p = signif(p, 3), z_model = round(z_model, 2),
    t_woman = round(t_woman, 2), df_woman, p_woman = signif(p_woman, 3),
    r = round(r, 4), ratio = round(ratio, 3), n, n_unions, n_marriages,
    rank, ref = is_reference
  )

# Every option off the curve that a display beside the curve holds, as one
# sentence: the options fitted alone at the reference settings, the shares
# of the life table, and the analyses of the Multi100 analysts on the file
# that SCORE built and on the same file with its 1995 rows rebuilt
f3 <- \(x, d = 3) sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
p_txt <- \(p) dplyr::if_else(p < 0.0001, "p < 0.0001", paste("p =", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))
big <- \(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
ref_b <- f3(curve$b[curve$is_reference])
sh <- \(cohort, col) 100 * shares[[col]][shares$cohort == cohort & shares$group_type == "all"]
an <- \(id, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id]
sf <- \(cycle, col) score_file[[col]][score_file$source == "SCORE file" & score_file$cycle == cycle]
display_fit <- displays |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    axis = changed, option,
    text = dplyr::case_when(
      option == "lpm" ~ sprintf(
        "A display beside the curve fits this option alone at the reference settings: %s, a monthly chance of marrying lower by %.1f percentage points, t = %s on %d df, %s, on %s person-months.",
        f3(b, 4), 100 * abs(b), f3(stat, 2), as.integer(df), p_txt(p), big(n)),
      .default = sprintf(
        "A display beside the curve fits this option alone at the reference settings: %s on the log scale, t = %s on %d df, %s, on %s person-months, against %s for the reference specification.",
        f3(b), f3(stat, 2), as.integer(df), p_txt(p), big(n), ref_b)
    )
  )
display_other <- tibble::tribble(
  ~axis, ~option, ~text,
  "outcome", "married_by_interview",
  sprintf("Weighted, %.1f%% of the unions of 1990–1995 had become a marriage by the interview, against %.1f%% of those of 2005–2010, whatever their length.",
          sh("1990-1995", "married_by_interview"), sh("2005-2010", "married_by_interview")),
  "outcome", "cumulative_3y",
  sprintf("From the life table: %.1f%% of the unions of 1990–1995 had become a marriage within three years, against %.1f%% of those of 2005–2010.",
          sh("1990-1995", "married_3y"), sh("2005-2010", "married_3y")),
  "outcome", "separation",
  sprintf("In Model 2 of the paper, refitted on the rebuilt unions, the period coefficient of separation is %s (published 0.071).",
          f3(repro$b[repro$model == 2 & repro$equation == "separation" & repro$term == "later"])),
  "histories", "score_file",
  sprintf("The 1995 cohort of the SCORE file holds %d unions, %d intact, %d marriages and %d separations, against 929 unions of the paper with 242, 340 and 347. On that file the test of 5X3KG gives chi-square = %s for more marriage in the later survey; with the 1995 rows rebuilt, %s for less.",
          sf("1995", "unions"), sf("1995", "intact"), sf("1995", "marriages"), sf("1995", "separations"),
          f3(an("5X3KG", "stat_refit"), 2), f3(an("5X3KG", "stat_repaired"), 2)),
  "unit", "unions",
  sprintf("N8ZYW analysed one row per woman of 1995 and 2006–2010 on the SCORE file: z = +%s for more marriage in the later survey; with the 1995 rows rebuilt, z = %s.",
          f3(an("N8ZYW", "stat_refit"), 2), f3(an("N8ZYW", "stat_repaired"), 2)),
  "unit", "rows_test",
  sprintf("5X3KG tested the shares of rows that record a marriage on the SCORE file: chi-square = %s for more marriage in the later survey; with the 1995 rows rebuilt, %s for less.",
          f3(an("5X3KG", "stat_refit"), 3), f3(an("5X3KG", "stat_repaired"), 2)),
  "comparison", "trend",
  sprintf("JDA15 fitted a trend over the five surveys on the SCORE file: z = %s for the yearly trend; with the 1995 rows rebuilt, z = %s. 73FDT regressed five survey coefficients on the year: F = %s.",
          f3(an("JDA15", "stat_refit"), 2), f3(an("JDA15", "stat_repaired"), 2), f3(an("73FDT", "stat_refit"), 2))
)
display <- dplyr::bind_rows(display_fit, display_other)

ojs_define(menu_raw = menu_js, curve_raw = curve_js, dev_raw = deviations,
           display_raw = display, pages_raw = pages)
```

The map lays out every decision that an analysis of the claim of the original authors (OAs) has to make, in the order in which an analyst meets them on the way from the data to a verdict: which women and unions enter the analysis, how their histories are built and how much each counts, which cohorts of unions are compared, what counts as progress to marriage and over what time, what the comparison holds constant, how the model treats the months of each union, and how the answer is tested and reported. Each decision shows all its options, those on the curve of 144 specifications and those that the course teaches off the curve because they answer another question, answer this one less well, check an answer that the curve already holds, or cannot be built from the data. The map opens on the reference specification, the model of the paper without its interaction of race-ethnicity and period.

Selecting an option rewrites the estimand statement, with the phrases that the choice changed marked, and opens a description of the option: what it estimates, whether it answers the claim, what it does to the estimate against its twins on the curve, and where in the course it is taught. For a selection on the curve, the verdict gives its estimate, its test with errors that follow the design of the surveys and its rank among the 144, and for a selection off the curve it gives the reason. The [specification menu](menu.qmd) gives the full reasoning. Nothing is fitted in the browser, and every number is read from the files under `data/` that the course pipeline writes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Data and constants of the map. This chunk displays nothing: a named cell
// whose value is not a DOM node would otherwise print as an inspector line.
menu = transpose(menu_raw)
curve = transpose(curve_raw)
devRows = transpose(dev_raw)
displays = transpose(display_raw)
VARY = ["cohorts", "horizon", "adjust", "weights", "time", "model"]
CHECK_AXES = ["errors", "scale"]
curveKey = d => VARY.map(a => d[a]).join("|")
curveIndex = new Map(curve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))

DM = {
  return {
    stages: [
      {id: "data", title: "The women and their unions", axes: ["sample", "histories", "short", "weights"], note: "Whose unions enter the analysis, how their histories are built, and how much each union counts."},
      {id: "comparison", title: "The cohorts", axes: ["comparison", "cohorts"], note: "Which surveys and which cohorts of unions are compared."},
      {id: "outcome", title: "The outcome", axes: ["outcome", "horizon"], note: "What counts as progress to marriage, and over what time."},
      {id: "adjustment", title: "The adjustment", axes: ["adjust", "education"], note: "What the comparison holds constant, and how education is coded."},
      {id: "model", title: "The model", axes: ["unit", "time", "model"], note: "Which rows the model takes, how it treats the time since the start of a union, and which model it is."},
      {id: "inference", title: "The test and the scale", axes: ["errors", "scale"], note: "How uncertain the estimate is said to be, and on which scale it is reported."}
    ],
    colour: {outcome: "#0e3b6a", horizon: "#0e3b6a", comparison: "#2a5d8f", cohorts: "#2a5d8f", adjust: "#4a78ab",
             sample: "#0f6b6b", weights: "#2b8585",
             histories: "#4a7a3f", education: "#4a7a3f", short: "#4a7a3f",
             unit: "#8c5a10", time: "#8c5a10", model: "#8c5a10", errors: "#7b6a8f", scale: "#7b6a8f"},
    levelOf: {sample: "l1", weights: "l1", comparison: "l1", cohorts: "l1", outcome: "l1", horizon: "l1", adjust: "l1",
              histories: "l2", education: "l2", short: "l2",
              unit: "l3", time: "l3", model: "l3", errors: "l3", scale: "l3"},
    levelName: {estimand: "Level 1 – Estimands", measurement: "Level 2 – Measurement", estimation: "Level 3 – Estimation"},
    levelShort: {estimand: "Level 1", measurement: "Level 2", estimation: "Level 3"},
    judgement: {kept: "On the curve", other_question: "Another question", weaker_answer: "A weaker answer", check: "A check", unavailable: "Not in the data"},
    domainB: [-1.12, 0.05],
    pairDomain: [-0.86, -0.6]
  };
}

// numbers as the site prints them: fixed decimals and a true minus sign
fmtB = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)
fmtShift = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : x > 0 ? "+" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(4)
fmtR = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)
fmtStat = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(2)
fmtN = x => Math.round(x).toLocaleString("en-GB")
fmtP = p => p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : p < 0.001 ? p.toFixed(4) : p.toFixed(3)
// "p = 0.021" or "p < 0.0001", so that a bound never follows an equals sign
pEq = p => p < 0.0001 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${fmtP(p)}`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
decisionMap = {
  const opt = (axis, code) => menu.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
  const optionsOf = axis => menu.filter(d => d.axis === axis);
  const ALL_AXES = DM.stages.flatMap(st => st.axes);
  const stageOf = axis => (DM.stages.find(st => st.axes.includes(axis)) || {}).id;
  const col = axis => DM.colour[axis];
  const el = (tag, attrs, ...kids) => {
    const n = document.createElement(tag);
    if (attrs) for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) {
      if (k === "class") n.className = v;
      else if (k === "text") n.textContent = v;
      else if (k === "style") n.setAttribute("style", v);
      else n.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
    for (const kid of kids) if (kid !== null && kid !== undefined) n.append(kid);
    return n;
  };
  const pageLink = file => el("a", {href: "../../" + file.replace(/\.qmd$/, ".html")}, pages_raw[file] || file);
  const baselineOf = axis => (devRows.find(d => d.axis === axis) || {}).baseline;

  // ---- state: one option per decision, starting from the reference specification
  const refRow = curve.find(d => d.ref === true);
  const REF = {};
  for (const a of ALL_AXES) REF[a] = (optionsOf(a).find(o => o.on_curve === true) || optionsOf(a)[0]).option;
  for (const a of VARY) REF[a] = refRow[a];
  let sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let latest = null;
  let prevText = null;

  const isOn = (s, a) => opt(a, s[a]).on_curve === true;
  const offAxes = s => ALL_AXES.filter(a => !isOn(s, a));
  const curveRowOf = s => { const k = curveIndex.get(curveKey(s)); return k === undefined ? null : curve[k]; };
  const recipe = d => VARY.map(a => opt(a, d[a]).label).join(" · ");

  // ---- the estimand statement, as segments that can be compared with the last one
  function statement(s) {
    const o = a => opt(a, s[a]);
    const cap = t => t.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + t.slice(1);
    const seg = (key, text) => ({key, text, lv: DM.levelOf[key]});
    return {
      question: [
        seg("sample", cap(o("sample").phrase)), ", ", seg("cohorts", o("cohorts").phrase), " ",
        seg("comparison", o("comparison").phrase), ", the change in ", seg("outcome", o("outcome").phrase), " ",
        seg("horizon", o("horizon").phrase), ", ", seg("weights", o("weights").phrase), ", ",
        seg("adjust", o("adjust").phrase), " (", seg("histories", o("histories").phrase), ", ",
        seg("education", o("education").phrase), ", ", seg("short", o("short").phrase), ")."
      ],
      method: [
        seg("model", o("model").phrase), " ", seg("unit", o("unit").phrase), ", ", seg("time", o("time").phrase),
        ", ", seg("errors", o("errors").phrase), " ", seg("scale", o("scale").phrase), "."
      ]
    };
  }
  function renderSegments(target, parts) {
    target.replaceChildren();
    for (const p of parts) {
      if (typeof p === "string") { target.append(p); continue; }
      const span = el("span", {class: `dm-seg ${p.lv}`, style: `--c:${col(p.key)}`, text: p.text});
      const changed = prevText !== null && prevText[p.key] !== undefined && prevText[p.key] !== p.text;
      target.append(changed ? el("mark", {class: "dm-changed"}, span) : span);
    }
  }

  // ---- what the selection gives
  function verdictOf(s) {
    const off = offAxes(s);
    const blocking = off.filter(a => !(CHECK_AXES.includes(a) && opt(a, s[a]).judgement === "check"));
    if (blocking.length > 0) return {kind: "off", axes: blocking};
    return {kind: "curve", d: curveRowOf(s), checks: off};
  }
  const statText = d => `t = ${fmtStat(d.stat)} on ${d.df} df`;
  function checkText(a, code, d) {
    if (a === "errors" && code === "woman") return `Clustered by woman, the same estimate has t = ${fmtStat(d.t_woman)} on ${fmtN(d.df_woman)} df, ${pEq(d.p_woman)}.`;
    if (a === "scale" && code === "ratio") return `As a ratio, the later cohort married at ${d.ratio.toFixed(2)} times the monthly chance of the earlier one.`;
    if (a === "scale" && code === "r") return `By the Multi100 rule, the conventional test converts to a partial correlation of ${fmtR(d.r)}.`;
    return "";
  }
  function shortVerdict(v) {
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d;
      const checks = v.checks.map(a => checkText(a, sel[a], d)).join(" ");
      return `On the curve: ${fmtB(d.b)} on the log scale (a ratio of ${d.ratio.toFixed(2)}), ${statText(d)} with errors that follow the design, ${pEq(d.p)}; ranked ${d.rank} of 144 from the largest decline.${checks ? " " + checks : ""}`;
    }
    return `Off the curve: ${v.axes.map(a => `${opt(a, sel[a]).decision.toLowerCase()} – ${opt(a, sel[a]).label} (${DM.judgement[opt(a, sel[a]).judgement].toLowerCase()})`).join("; ")}.`;
  }
  function longVerdict(v) {
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d;
      const parts = [`The selection is one of the 144 specifications on the curve. Its estimate is ${fmtB(d.b)} on the log scale, so that the later cohort married at ${d.ratio.toFixed(2)} times the monthly chance of the earlier one, on ${fmtN(d.n)} person-months of ${fmtN(d.n_unions)} unions with ${fmtN(d.n_marriages)} marriages, with ${statText(d)} and ${pEq(d.p)} under errors that follow the design of the surveys; conventional errors would give z = ${fmtStat(d.z_model)}. Ranked from the largest decline, it is number ${d.rank} of the 144.`];
      for (const a of v.checks) parts.push(checkText(a, sel[a], d));
      return parts.join(" ");
    }
    const reasons = v.axes.map(a => {
      const o = opt(a, sel[a]);
      return `${o.decision} – ${o.label}: ${o.reason}`;
    }).join(" ");
    let txt = `The curve holds no analysis with this selection. ${reasons}`;
    if (v.axes.length === 1) {
      const a = v.axes[0];
      const disp = displays.find(d => d.axis === a && d.option === sel[a]);
      const onVary = VARY.every(x => isOn(sel, x));
      if (a === "errors" && sel[a] === "model" && onVary) {
        const d = curveRowOf(sel);
        txt += ` The curve stores the conventional test of every specification: for this one, ${fmtB(d.b)} with z = ${fmtStat(d.z_model)}, against t = ${fmtStat(d.stat)} on ${d.df} df with errors that follow the design.`;
      } else if (disp) {
        txt += ` ${disp.text}`;
      }
    } else {
      txt += " Each option off the curve is taught on its own, so this combination was never fitted.";
    }
    return txt + " The burgundy marks are the specifications on the curve that share every other choice.";
  }

  // ---- the map
  const stageEls = {};
  const chipEls = [];
  const verdictBox = el("p", {class: "dm-verdict", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const resetBtn = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-reset"}, "Back to the reference specification");
  const stagesBox = el("div", {class: "dm-stages"});
  DM.stages.forEach((st, si) => {
    const box = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": `dm-stage-${st.id}`},
      el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(si + 1)),
        el("h3", {id: `dm-stage-${st.id}`}, st.title)),
      el("p", {class: "dm-stage-note"}, st.note));
    for (const axis of st.axes) {
      const opts = optionsOf(axis);
      const first = opts[0];
      const nameId = `dm-dec-${axis}`;
      const group = el("div", {class: "dm-chips", role: "group", "aria-labelledby": nameId});
      for (const o of opts) {
        const tip = o.on_curve ? `${o.label}: on the curve` : `${o.label}: off the curve, ${DM.judgement[o.judgement].toLowerCase()}`;
        const b = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-chip" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${col(axis)}`,
                                "aria-pressed": "false", title: tip, "aria-label": tip, "data-axis": axis, "data-option": o.option}, o.label);
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          const before = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          sel[axis] = o.option;
          latest = axis;
          update(st.id);
          const after = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
        });
        chipEls.push({b, axis, code: o.option});
        group.append(b);
      }
      box.append(el("div", {class: "dm-decision"},
        el("div", {class: "dm-decision-name", id: nameId}, first.decision,
          el("span", {class: "lv", style: `color:${col(axis)}`}, DM.levelShort[first.level])),
        group));
    }
    stageEls[st.id] = box;
    stagesBox.append(box);
  });
  const verdictStage = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": "dm-stage-verdict"},
    el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(DM.stages.length + 1)),
      el("h3", {id: "dm-stage-verdict"}, "The verdict")),
    verdictBox, resetBtn);
  stagesBox.append(verdictStage);
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const before = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
    latest = null;
    update(null);
    const after = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
  });

  // ---- the panel: statement, the selected option, its twins, the curve
  const statementP = el("p", {class: "dm-statement estimand", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const methodP = el("p", {class: "dm-method"});
  const changedNote = el("p", {class: "dm-small"});
  const optionBox = el("div");
  const pairBox = el("div");
  const curveBox = el("div");
  const panel = el("div", {class: "dm-panel", role: "region", "aria-label": "The selection and its results"},
    el("h3", {}, "The estimand statement"), statementP, methodP, changedNote,
    el("h3", {}, "The selected option"), optionBox,
    el("h3", {}, "Against its twins on the curve"), pairBox,
    el("h3", {}, "The curve of 144"), curveBox);
  const side = el("div", {class: "dm-side"});
  const topSlot = el("div");
  const layout = el("div", {class: "dm-layout"}, el("div", {}, topSlot, stagesBox), side);

  const legend = el("div", {class: "dm-legend"},
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0e3b6a"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0f6b6b"}), DM.levelName.estimand),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#4a7a3f"}), DM.levelName.measurement),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#8c5a10"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#7b6a8f"}), DM.levelName.estimation),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample"}, "solid"), "on the curve"),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample off"}, "dashed"), "in the course, off the curve"));

  const wide = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1100px)");
  function place(stageId) {
    if (wide.matches) { if (panel.parentNode !== side) side.append(panel); return; }
    if (stageId === null || stageId === undefined) { if (panel.parentNode !== topSlot) topSlot.append(panel); return; }
    const anchor = stageId === "verdict" ? verdictStage : stageEls[stageId];
    if (anchor.nextSibling !== panel) anchor.after(panel);
  }

  // ---- charts
  function curveChart(width) {
    const onVary = VARY.filter(a => isOn(sel, a));
    const match = curve.filter(d => onVary.every(a => d[a] === sel[a]));
    const matchSet = new Set(match.map(d => d.spec_id));
    const showLatest = latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest);
    const latestRows = showLatest ? curve.filter(d => d[latest] === sel[latest] && !matchSet.has(d.spec_id)) : [];
    const latestSet = new Set(latestRows.map(d => d.spec_id));
    const base = curve.filter(d => !matchSet.has(d.spec_id) && !latestSet.has(d.spec_id));
    const tip = d => `${recipe(d)}\n${fmtB(d.b)} on the log scale, ${statText(d)}, ${pEq(d.p)}`;
    const dots = (data, stroke, op, r, sw) => [
      Plot.ruleX(data, {x: "rank", y1: "lo", y2: "hi", stroke, strokeOpacity: op * 0.35, strokeWidth: sw}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p < 0.05), {x: "rank", y: "b", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: tip}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p >= 0.05), {x: "rank", y: "b", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: tip})
    ];
    const ref = curve.filter(d => d.ref === true);
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(230, Math.min(320, Math.round(width * 0.5))), marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 38,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: "The curve of 144 specifications, with the current selection marked",
      x: {domain: [0, 145], label: "144 specifications, ranked from the largest decline →", ticks: 4},
      y: {domain: DM.domainB, label: "↑ Coefficient of the later cohort (log scale)", grid: true, ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        ...dots(base, "#1d2731", 0.3, 3, 0.7),
        ...dots(latestRows, col(latest || "cohorts"), 0.7, 3.2, 0.9),
        ...dots(match, "#8b1538", 1, 4.8, 1.5),
        Plot.text(ref, {x: "rank", y: "b", text: () => "reference", dy: -16, fontSize: 10, fill: "#1d2731"})
      ]
    });
  }
  function pairData(axis, code) {
    const base = baselineOf(axis);
    const others = VARY.filter(a => a !== axis);
    const key = d => others.map(a => d[a]).join("|");
    const baseMap = new Map(curve.filter(d => d[axis] === base).map(d => [key(d), d]));
    const rows = code === base ? curve.filter(d => d[axis] !== base) : curve.filter(d => d[axis] === code);
    return rows.map(d => ({x: baseMap.get(key(d)).b, y: d.b, s: d.p < 0.05, row: d, twin: baseMap.get(key(d))}));
  }
  function pairChart(width, axis, code, data) {
    const c = col(axis);
    const others = VARY.filter(a => a !== axis);
    const isSel = d => others.every(a => d.row[a] === sel[a]) && (code === baselineOf(axis) || d.row[axis] === code);
    const selPair = isOn(sel, axis) ? data.filter(isSel) : [];
    const tip = d => `${recipe(d.row)}\n${fmtB(d.x)} → ${fmtB(d.y)}`;
    const [lo, hi] = DM.pairDomain;
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(240, Math.min(340, Math.round(width * 0.6))), marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 40,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: `Each specification on the curve set against its twin with ${opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label}`,
      x: {domain: [lo, hi], label: `with ${opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label.toLowerCase()} (log scale) →`, ticks: 5},
      y: {domain: [lo, hi], label: "↑ with the other option (log scale)", ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        Plot.line([[lo, lo], [hi, hi]], {stroke: "#5b6b78", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        Plot.dot(data, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 3.4, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke: c, strokeOpacity: 0.7, strokeWidth: 1, title: tip}),
        Plot.dot(selPair, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 6, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke: "#8b1538", strokeWidth: 1.8, title: tip})
      ]
    });
  }

  // ---- the selected option, in words and numbers
  const curveRange = [d3.min(curve, d => d.b), d3.max(curve, d => d.b)];
  function summaryText(axis, code, o) {
    const out = [];
    if (!o.on_curve) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The course does not cross this option with the curve, so there are no twins to set it against. The verdict below gives the reason and, where a display beside the curve holds the option, its result."));
      return out;
    }
    if (!VARY.includes(axis)) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Every specification on the curve uses this option, so there is nothing on the curve to set it against. On the curve the 144 estimates run from ${fmtB(curveRange[0])} to ${fmtB(curveRange[1])} on the log scale, and all are significant at 5% with errors that follow the design of the surveys.`));
      return out;
    }
    const base = baselineOf(axis);
    const baseLabel = opt(axis, base).label;
    if (code !== base) {
      const r = devRows.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Against their twins with ${baseLabel.toLowerCase()}, the ${r.n_pairs} specifications with this option move the estimate by ${fmtShift(r.shift_mean)} on average, from ${fmtShift(r.shift_min)} to ${fmtShift(r.shift_max)}, and ${Math.round(100 * r.sig_share)}% of them stay significant at 5%. A positive shift moves the estimate towards zero.`));
    } else {
      const alts = devRows.filter(d => d.axis === axis && d.option !== base)
        .map(d => `${opt(axis, d.option).label.toLowerCase()} by ${fmtShift(d.shift_mean)} on average`).join(", ");
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `This is the option against which the others of the decision are compared. Swapped in on twin specifications, the alternatives move the estimate as follows: ${alts}.`));
    }
    return out;
  }

  function renderOption(width) {
    optionBox.replaceChildren();
    pairBox.replaceChildren();
    if (latest === null) {
      optionBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The map opens on the reference specification: the cohorts of the paper, every observed month, age, race-ethnicity and education held constant, the survey weights, the months since the start as a straight line, and a multinomial logit. Select any option on the map to read what it estimates and whether it answers the claim."));
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "Once an option of a decision that varies on the curve is selected, a chart here sets each specification against its twin that differs only in that decision."));
      return;
    }
    const axis = latest, code = sel[axis], o = opt(axis, code), c = col(axis);
    optionBox.append(
      el("p", {class: "dm-option-title"}, `${o.decision}: ${o.label}`),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge", style: `--c:${c}`}, DM.levelName[o.level]),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${o.on_curve ? "#1d2731" : "#8b1538"}`}, DM.judgement[o.judgement]),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, "What it estimates. "), o.estimates),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, o.on_curve ? "Why it is on the curve. " : "Why it is off the curve. "), o.explanation),
      el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Taught on ", pageLink(o.page), "."));
    for (const p of summaryText(axis, code, o)) pairBox.append(p);
    if (o.on_curve && VARY.includes(axis)) {
      const data = pairData(axis, code);
      const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
      box.append(pairChart(width, axis, code, data));
      pairBox.append(box);
      const baseLabel = opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label.toLowerCase();
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, code === baselineOf(axis)
        ? `Each mark is one pair: a specification with ${baseLabel}, placed horizontally by its estimate, and its twin with another option of the decision, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks above it lie closer to zero. The burgundy marks are the pairs of the current selection.`
        : `Each mark is one pair: a specification with ${baseLabel}, placed horizontally by its estimate, and its twin with ${o.label.toLowerCase()}, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks above it lie closer to zero. The burgundy mark is the pair of the current selection.`));
    }
  }

  let lastWidth = 0;
  function drawPanel() {
    const width = Math.max(280, Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34));
    lastWidth = width;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    renderOption(width);
    curveBox.replaceChildren();
    const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
    box.append(curveChart(width));
    curveBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, longVerdict(v)), box,
      el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, `Each mark is one of the 144 specifications on the curve of the claim, ranked from the largest decline, with its 95% confidence interval from errors that follow the design of the surveys; below zero, the cohabiting couples of the later cohort married less often. Open circles are significant at 5%. Burgundy marks are the specifications that match every on-curve choice of the selection${latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest) ? `, and the coloured marks are the other specifications that share the option selected last (${opt(latest, sel[latest]).label})` : ""}. The ink label marks the reference specification.`));
  }

  function update(stageId) {
    for (const {b, axis, code} of chipEls) b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", sel[axis] === code ? "true" : "false");
    const st = statement(sel);
    renderSegments(statementP, st.question);
    renderSegments(methodP, st.method);
    const nowText = {};
    for (const p of [...st.question, ...st.method]) if (typeof p !== "string") nowText[p.key] = p.text;
    const anyChanged = prevText !== null && Object.keys(nowText).some(k => prevText[k] !== nowText[k]);
    changedNote.textContent = (anyChanged ? "The marked phrases are the ones that the latest choice changed. " : "")
      + "Bold phrases state the question (Level 1), green phrases say how its parts are measured (Level 2), and the second sentence says how the answer is reached (Level 3).";
    prevText = nowText;
    verdictBox.textContent = shortVerdict(verdictOf(sel));
    place(stageId);
    drawPanel();
  }

  const root = el("div", {class: "dm"}, legend, layout);
  update(null);
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    const w = Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34);
    if (w > 0 && Math.abs(w - lastWidth) > 24) { place(latest === null ? null : stageOf(latest)); drawPanel(); }
  });
  ro.observe(root);
  const onMedia = () => { place(latest === null ? null : stageOf(latest)); drawPanel(); };
  wide.addEventListener("change", onMedia);
  invalidation.then(() => { ro.disconnect(); wide.removeEventListener("change", onMedia); });
  return root;
}
```

The three levels of the map are those of the [specification menu](menu.qmd#level-estimand): a Level 1 choice changes the question, a Level 2 choice changes how its parts are measured, and a Level 3 choice changes how the answer is reached. Two decisions sit in a stage with decisions of another level. The union histories are built with the data, at the first stage, but they are a Level 2 decision, because rebuilding the unions from the dates of the surveys and taking them from the file that SCORE built answer the same question with different measurements; the [case study](index.qmd#sec-1995) shows how far apart those measurements are for 1995. The coding of education is chosen with the adjustment, and it too only changes how a control is measured, while the choice of what to hold constant is a Level 1 decision, because it fixes whether the coefficient describes cohabitors as they were or the change within groups of the same age, race-ethnicity and education. The [specification menu](menu.qmd#adjustment) sets out, with the causal graph, why the three sets on the curve answer different readings of the claim.
